about.title: Personal Injury Help in Livingston, California
about.longDescription: Livingston is a close-knit farming community, but its roads carry a steady stream of daily traffic, and that traffic sometimes leads to crashes. In the most recent reporting year, Livingston recorded 35 injury collisions, 43 injured people, and 3 traffic deaths. Public crash records show collisions cluster along Hammatt Avenue, Walnut Avenue, F Street, and Main Street, with Fridays between 4 and 6 p.m. showing more reports than other times. If you were hurt in one of these incidents, sorting out medical bills, missed work, and insurance calls can feel overwhelming on top of recovering physically. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people in Livingston with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened and explain your options. We are not a law firm, and we don't provide legal advice ourselves — we simply make the introduction. Attorneys in our network take cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for you. Reaching out costs nothing and puts you in touch with someone who can look at the specifics of your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why Act Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: The Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim, but claims against a government agency can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can mean losing your right to recover at all.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be Black and White
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly at fault — your share of fault simply reduces the amount, it doesn't eliminate your claim.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in typical injury cases, so these losses can be fully considered when valuing a claim.

items.title: You Don't Pay Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if they recover money for you — there's no hourly billing or retainer required.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have two years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a city vehicle, the notice deadline can be as short as six months, so it's important not to delay.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your total recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Livingston?
items.answer: Public crash records show higher collision counts along Hammatt Avenue, Walnut Avenue, F Street, and Main Street, with more reports occurring on Fridays between 4 and 6 p.m. These are neutral counts from public records, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge any fees?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent attorney. We are not a law firm, and the attorneys we connect you with work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they recover money for you.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In most ordinary personal injury cases in California, there is no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. This is different from some other types of claims, such as certain medical malpractice cases.
